Vera flicked on her sub’s external comms, her fingers trembling slightly against the cool metal console. The static cracked, then melted into Rhys’s low, unmistakable voice.

"I thought I lost your signal off the Mariana Trench," he said, the dark expanse of the ocean amplifying the intimacy of his tone.

"I wasn't hiding, Rhys," Vera replied, catching her breath as she looked through the thick acrylic viewport. Just feet away, his amber eyes locked onto hers through the dark glass. "I had a mission."

"So did I," he murmured. "My mission was you."

A sudden tremor shivered through the seabed beneath them. Red warning lights bathed Vera's cockpit in a crimson glow—a hydrothermal vent was rupturing right between their vessels. The turbulent pressure currents threatened to slam their hulls together, hard enough to crack the reinforced titanium.

"Vera, disengage! Pull back!" Rhys commanded, his voice sharp with panic, professional rivalry instantly evaporating into pure instinct to protect her.

Instead of retreating, Vera gripped the thruster controls, matching his sub's precise frequency to stabilize both ships against the surging current. "Not a chance, Commander. We balance each other, remember?"

Through the violent swirling sediment and flashing alarm lights, Rhys smiled—a rare, breathtaking sight that made the cold abyss feel impossibly warm. He maneuvered his sub closer, aligning their airlock docking collars with terrifying precision until a heavy, metallic *thunk* echoed through both hulls. 

The pressure equalized. The seal was locked.

"I'm coming over," Rhys announced, his voice dropping to a husky whisper over the radio. "And I'm not letting you go this time."

Vera unbuckled her harness, her chest heaving as she stood before the inner hatch door, listening to the heavy manual wheel begin to turn from the other side.

Come back for the next part tomorrow.
